The 2012–13 season was [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea Football Club]]'s 99th competitive season, 24th consecutive season in the top flight of English [[association football|football]], 21st consecutive season in the [[Premier League]], and 107th year in existence as a [[Football team|football club]]. Chelsea's victory in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League]] for the first time in their history qualified them for the season's [[UEFA Super Cup]] and [[FIFA Club World Cup]], although through finishing third in their Champions League group Chelsea competed in the [[UEFA Europa League]] for the first time since the 2002–03 season – then known as the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]].
==Season summary==
On 13 June 2012, [[Roberto Di Matteo]] signed a two-year contract, becoming Chelsea's permanent manager,<ref name="di matteo two">{{cite news|title=Di Matteo signs two-year contract |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2810782 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130624214041/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2810782 |url-status=dead |archive-date=24 June 2013 |publisher=Chelsea F.C |date=13 June 2012 }}</ref> having been appointed as [[Interim management|interim manager]] after the sacking of [[André Villas-Boas]] during the [[2011–12 in English football|2011–12 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Villas-Boas sacked by Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17250464|work=BBC Sport|date=4 March 2012}}</ref> However, on 21 November 2012, [[Roberto Di Matteo|Di Matteo]] was sacked<ref name="statement di matteo">{{cite news|title=Statement on Roberto Di Matteo |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2986865/title/statement-on-roberto-di-matteo |publisher=Chelsea F.C |date=21 November 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121122225716/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2986865/title/statement-on-roberto-di-matteo |archive-date=22 November 2012 }}</ref> after a 3–0 loss away to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the [[UEFA Champions League]], with [[Rafael Benítez]] replacing him as [[Interim management|interim manager]] until the end of the season.<ref name="benitez in">{{cite news|title=Benitez appointed|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2987554/title/benitez-appointed|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=21 November 2012}}</ref> On 15 May 2013, Chelsea won their first and only silverware of the season, winning the [[2013 UEFA Europa League Final|Europa League final]] against Portuguese side [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]]. They finished the [[Premier League]] season in third place.

The season was the first since [[2003–04 Chelsea F.C. season|2003–04]] without [[Didier Drogba]] and the first since [[2006–07 Chelsea F.C. season|2006–07]] without [[Nicolas Anelka]], both of whom joined [[Shanghai Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Shenhua]].

===June===
[[File:Hazard vs Norwich (crop).jpg|thumb|right|200px|{{center|On 4 June [[Eden Hazard]] became Chelsea's first signing of the new season, joining for £32 million from [[Lille OSC|Lille]].}}]]
Excluding players such as [[Marko Marin]], who was signed during the previous season, Chelsea made their first signing of the new campaign on 4 June, signing Belgian international winger [[Eden Hazard]] from [[Lille OSC|Lille]] for an undisclosed fee rumoured to be £32 million.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18324490 "Eden Hazard: Chelsea complete transfer of Lille midfielder"]. ''BBC Sport''. 4 June 2012.</ref> Three days later, the club lost a bid to purchase nearby [[Battersea Power Station]] which they considered converting to a stadium and make it their new home ground.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea Statement on Battersea Power Station |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2804528 |work=Chelseafc.com |date=7 June 2012 |access-date=21 June 2012 }}</ref>

[[Roberto Di Matteo]], who had won the Champions League in the previous season as interim manager, was given a two-year contract as first-team manager on 13 June.<ref name="di matteo two"/> On 20 June, [[Didier Drogba]], who scored more than 150 goals for Chelsea in his eight seasons, completed his free transfer to Chinese club [[Shanghai Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Shenhua]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Drogba confirms China move|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2817183 |work=Chelseafc.com |date=20 June 2012 |access-date=21 June 2012 }}</ref>

===July===
At the [[City of Westminster Magistrates' Court|Westminster Magistrates' Court]], [[John Terry]] was found not guilty of racially abusing [[Anton Ferdinand]]. The district judge concluded "there being a doubt, the only verdict the court can record is one of not guilty."<ref>{{cite web|last=Levene |first=Dan |url=http://www.fulhamchronicle.co.uk/london-chelsea-fc/2012/07/13/terry-not-guilty-of-racism-64767-31390019/ |title=Terry not guilty of racism|work=[[Fulham & Hammersmith Chronicle]] |date=13 July 2012 |access-date=28 July 2012}}</ref> Chelsea announced a "global energy partnership" with Russian energy firm [[Gazprom]] in a three-year deal with a value deemed "commercially confidential", which will help reduce the club's deficits under [[UEFA Financial Fair Play Regulations]].<ref>[http://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com/Daily/Issues/2012/07/18/Marketing-and-Sponsorship/Gazprom-Chelsea.aspx "Chelsea Signs Three-Year Deal With Russian Energy Company Gazprom"]. ''SportsBusiness Daily''. 18 July 2012.</ref> On 28 July, the club completed the signing of Brazilian midfielder [[Oscar (footballer, born 1991)|Oscar]] from [[Sport Club Internacional|Internacional]] for a reported £25 million fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/jul/25/chelsea-sign-oscar-brazil-internacional |title=Chelsea complete signing of Brazil midfielder Oscar from Internacional|work=[[The Guardian]] |date=25 July 2012 |access-date=28 July 2012}}</ref>

===August===
On 2 August, [[Kevin De Bruyne]] was sent on a season-long loan deal to [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] of the German [[Bundesliga]].<ref name="de bruyne werder">{{cite web|title=De Bruyne loan completed|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2869398|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=2 August 2012|access-date=6 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130906093314/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2869398|archive-date=6 September 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> Chelsea played their first competitive match of the season in the [[FA Community Shield|Community Shield]] at [[Villa Park]] on 12 August, but lost 3–2 to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] and had [[Branislav Ivanović]] sent off.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19133978 "Chelsea 2–3 Man City"]. ''BBC Sport''. 12 August 2012.</ref> The club officially announced the signings of Spanish right-back [[César Azpilicueta]] from [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] and forward [[Victor Moses]] from [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] on 24 August.<ref name="azpi move">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2898781 |title=Azpilicueta Signs |publisher=Chelsea F.C |date=24 August 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120830171700/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2898781 |archive-date=30 August 2012 }}</ref><ref name="moses move">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2899458/title/moses-transfer-completed|title=Moses transfer completed|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=24 August 2012|access-date=24 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120830172555/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2899458/title/moses-transfer-completed|archive-date=30 August 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Chelsea's [[2012–13 Premier League|Premier League campaign]] began on 19 August with a 0–2 victory in an away match against Wigan Athletic. Both goals came in the first ten minutes, the first from Branislav Ivanović and then a [[Frank Lampard]] penalty after [[Eden Hazard]] was fouled.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19231340 "Wigan 0–2 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 19 August 2013.</ref> The Blues won their second match 4–2 against [[Reading F.C.|Reading]],<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19279583 "Chelsea 4–2 Reading"]. ''BBC Sport''. 22 August 2012.</ref> and made it three wins out of three with a 2–0 win over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19304403 "Chelsea 2–0 Newcastle"]. ''BBC Sport''. 25 August 2012.</ref> Chelsea lost 4–1 to [[Atlético Madrid]] in the [[2012 UEFA Super Cup]], for whom [[Radamel Falcao]] scored a hat-trick.<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/aug/31/chelsea-atletico-madrid-live-mbm "Chelsea v Atlético Madrid – as it happened"]. ''The Guardian''. 31 August 2012.</ref>

On transfer deadline day, [[Michael Essien]] left on a season-long loan deal with [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], signed by [[José Mourinho]], who had previously signed him for Chelsea.<ref name="Essien Loaned to Real Madrid">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2906850/title/essien-loaned-to-real-madrid |title=Essien loaned to Real Madrid |publisher=Chelsea F.C |date=31 August 2012 |access-date=31 August 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902175405/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2906850/title/essien-loaned-to-real-madrid |archive-date=2 September 2012}}</ref> Two more players left Chelsea on season-long loans the same day, as [[Yossi Benayoun]] went to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] and [[Gaël Kakuta]] joined Dutch club [[Vitesse Arnhem]].

===September===
On 3 September Chelsea sold Portuguese midfielder [[Raul Meireles]] to Turkish club [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] for £8 million, due to Turkey's transfer window closing later than England's.<ref name="meireles-chelsea">{{cite news|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2909772/title/meireles-departs-for-turkey|title=Meireles departs for Turkey|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=3 September 2012|access-date=4 September 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905020032/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2909772/title/meireles-departs-for-turkey|archive-date=5 September 2012}}</ref> [[Ryan Bertrand]] signed a five-year contract to extend his career at Chelsea until the summer of 2017.<ref>[http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2911095/title/long-term-deal-for-bertrand "Long-term deal for Bertrand"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120907015112/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2911095/title/long-term-deal-for-bertrand |date=7 September 2012 }}. Chelsea F.C. 5 September 2012.</ref> Chelsea's run of three consecutive league wins from the start of the season ended on 15 September as they drew 0–0 away to [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]]. Before the game, [[Anton Ferdinand]] refused to shake [[John Terry]]'s and [[Ashley Cole]]'s hand in the pre-match handshake.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19528273 "QPR 0–0 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 15 September 2012.</ref>

Chelsea began their defence of the [[UEFA Champions League]] on 19 September, at home to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], and went 2–0 up with [[Oscar (footballer, born 1991)|Oscar]]'s first goals for the club before Juventus equalised.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19567014 "Chelsea 2–2 Juventus"]. ''BBC Sport''. 19 September 2012.</ref> Brazilian defender [[David Luiz]] signed a new five-year contract at the club.<ref>"{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130419213232/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19689655|title=BBC Sport – David Luiz signs new five-year with Chelsea}}". ''BBC Sport''. 22 September 2012.</ref> On 22 September, Ashley Cole was the unlikely hero as Chelsea scored a dramatic late winner to defeat [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] at home.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19615097 "Chelsea 1–0 Stoke"]. ''BBC Sport''. 22 September 2012.</ref> Chelsea beat [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] 6–0 in the [[2012–13 Football League Cup|League Cup]], with goals coming from [[Gary Cahill]], [[Juan Mata]], [[Fernando Torres]] and first goals for [[Victor Moses]], [[Oriol Romeu]] and Ryan Bertrand.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19632463 "Chelsea 6–0 Wolves"]. ''BBC Sport''. 25 September 2012.</ref>

Chelsea captain John Terry was banned for four games and fined £220,000 by the [[Football Association|FA]] for racially abusing QPR defender Anton Ferdinand.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19723020 "John Terry banned and fined by FA over Anton Ferdinand incident"]. ''BBC Sport''. 27 September 2012.</ref> On 29 September, Chelsea became the first team of the season to defeat [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at the [[Emirates Stadium]], with a 1–2 victory which put the Blues three points clear at the top after six matches.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20121223103155/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19684245|title="Arsenal 1–2 Chelsea"}}. ''BBC Sport''. 29 September 2012.</ref>

===October===
Chelsea won for the first time in their [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|2012–13 Champions League campaign]] by defeating Danish champions [[FC Nordsjælland|Nordsjælland]] 0–4 away with goals from [[Ramires]], David Luiz and two from playmaker Juan Mata.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19709698 "FC Nordsjaelland 0–4 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 2 October 2012.</ref> On 6 October, Fernando Torres, Frank Lampard, Eden Hazard and Branislav Ivanović scored in Chelsea's 4–1 home victory over [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]],<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19776324 "Chelsea 4–1 Norwich"]. ''BBC Sport''. 6 October 2012.</ref> before travelling to London rivals [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] on 20 October for a 2–4 victory, with goals from [[Gary Cahill]], [[Daniel Sturridge]] and two from Juan Mata. This was Chelsea's first victory at Tottenham's [[White Hart Lane]] since the FA Cup Quarter-Final Replay in 2007.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19939634 "Tottenham 2–4 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 20 October 2012.</ref>

On 23 October, Chelsea lost their first Champions League match for the season as they lost 2–1 to [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] in Ukraine.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19958153 "Shakhtar Donetsk 2–1 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 23 October 2012. Retrieved 9 June 2013.</ref> Both Branislav Ivanović and Fernando Torres were sent off in Chelsea's home Premier League match against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on 28 October, a game which saw Chelsea go 0–2 down and equalise before a controversially late winner from United's [[Javier Hernández]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20020062 "Chelsea 2–3 Manchester United"]. ''BBC Sport''. 28 October 2012.</ref> Later, Chelsea Lodged an official complaint based on [[Mikel John Obi]] claiming the referee [[Mark Clattenburg]] had used "inappropriate language."<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/oct/28/mark-clattenburg-accused-racial-slur-chelsea "Mark Clattenburg accused of racial slur during Chelsea v Manchester United"]. ''The Guardian''. 28 October 2012.</ref> Clattenburg was cleared of the accusations on 22 November.<ref name="cleared">[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20420934 "Mark Clattenburg cleared by FA as Chelsea's Mikel is charged"]. ''BBC Sport''. 22 November 2012.</ref><ref name="statement2211">[http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2988432/title/statement-on-clattenburg-decision "Statement on Clattenburg decision"]. Chelsea F.C. 22 November 2012.</ref> On 31 October, Chelsea defeated Manchester United 5–4 in the [[2012–13 Football League Cup#Fourth round|fourth round of the League Cup]], coming from behind three times to force extra time before goals from Daniel Sturridge and Ramires secured the win for the Blues.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20053672 "Chelsea 5–4 Manchester United (aet)"]. ''BBC Sport''. 31 October 2012.</ref>

===November===
[[File:Rafaelbenitez.jpg|thumb|right|200px|{{center|[[Rafael Benítez]] was appointed in November as Chelsea's interim coach until the end of the season.}}]]
Chelsea playmaker Juan Mata was voted [[Premier League Player of the Month]] for October after scoring three goals and contributing three assists.<ref name="ReferenceA">[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20220615 "Sir Alex Ferguson & Juan Mata win monthly league awards"]. ''BBC Sport''. 6 November 2012.</ref> On 3 November, Chelsea fell from first place in the Premier League (held since 25 August) after a 1–1 draw at [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]]'s [[Liberty Stadium]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20107634 "Swansea 1–1 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 3 November 2012.</ref> Chelsea kept up hope of qualifying from their Champions League group by defeating Shakhtar Donetsk 3–2 at home with an injury-time winner from Victor Moses on 7 November. The victory put Chelsea on top of Group E with two games to play.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20150427 "Chelsea 3–2 Shakhtar Donetsk"]. ''BBC Sport''. 7 November 2012.</ref> Chelsea then failed to win for their fourth Premier League match in a row after [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] beat them 2–1 away at [[The Hawthorns]] on 17 November. The defeat widened the gap between Chelsea and first-place by four points.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20278397 "West Brom 2–1 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 17 November 2012.</ref>

[[Roberto Di Matteo]] was dismissed from his position on 21 November, the morning after a 3–0 away defeat to Juventus, which put Chelsea at risk of being eliminated from the Champions League,<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20308128 "Juventus 3–0 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 20 November 2012.</ref> ending a 262-day tenure which saw him win the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League]] and the [[2011–12 FA Cup]] for Chelsea.<ref name="statement di matteo"/><ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20423905 "Roberto Di Matteo sacked by Chelsea after Juventus defeat"]. ''BBC Sport''. 21 November 2012.</ref><ref>[http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11668/8264374/Chelsea-sack-manager-Roberto-Di-Matteo-after-poor-run-of-form "Chelsea sack manager Roberto Di Matteo after poor run of form"]. ''[[Sky Sports]]''. 21 November 2012.</ref> On the same day, former [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] manager [[Rafael Benítez]] was appointed as the club's [[Interim management|interim manager]] until the end of the season.<ref name="benitez in"/><ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20427966 "Rafael Benitez replaces Roberto Di Matteo as Chelsea manager"]. ''BBC sport''. 21 November 2012.</ref> His first act of his tenure was to name Dutchman [[Boudewijn Zenden]], a former Chelsea midfielder who had played under him at Liverpool, as his assistant.<ref>[http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11668/8270568/Rafael-Benitez-has-appointed-Boudewijn-Zenden-as-his-assistant-at-Chelsea "Rafael Benitez has appointed Boudewijn Zenden as his assistant at Chelsea"]. ''Sky Sports''. 22 November 2012.</ref>

Chelsea midfielder Mikel John Obi was charged with misconduct by the FA after his allegations of racial abuse against referee Mark Clattenburg in the October fixture against Manchester United were found to be baseless.<ref name="cleared" /><ref name="statement2211"/> Mikel later received a three-match ban and a £60,000 fine as punishment for his behaviour after the match against Manchester United in October.<ref>[http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3002352/title/mikel-suspended "Mikel suspended"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121208221918/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3002352/title/mikel-suspended |date=8 December 2012 }}. Chelsea F.C. 6 December 2012.</ref><ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20631964 "John Mikel Obi banned for Mark Clattenburg threats"]. ''BBC Sport''. 6 December 2012.</ref> Benítez's first game in charge was a goalless draw with [[2011–12 Premier League]] winners Manchester City on 25 November. Despite not scoring, Chelsea kept their first clean sheet since the 1–0 win over Stoke City on 22 September.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20383491 "Chelsea 0–0 Manchester City"]. ''BBC Sport''. 25 November 2012.</ref> The club's next game, a [[West London derby#Chelsea vs Fulham derby|West London Derby]] against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], again ended 0–0, leaving Chelsea seven points off the top and six off second place.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20422485 "Chelsea 0–0 Fulham"]. ''BBC Sport''. 28 November 2012.</ref>

===December===
On 1 December, Benítez lost for the first time in his Chelsea tenure after Chelsea were beaten 3–1 away to London rivals [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20474474 "West Ham 3–1 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 1 December 2012.</ref> Three days later, Chelsea confirmed the signing of [[Brazil national under-20 football team|Brazil under-20]] right back [[Wallace Oliveira dos Santos|Wallace]] from [[Rio de Janeiro]]-based club [[Fluminense Football Club|Fluminense]] for an undisclosed fee. The option to sign a player from Fluminense was part of the deal that saw former Chelsea midfielder [[Deco]] join the team in 2010.<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/8895238.stm "Fluminense announce signing of Portugal midfielder Deco"]. ''BBC Sport''. 7 August 2010.</ref><ref name="BBC-wallace">[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20601358 "Chelsea to sign Brazilian Wallace from Fluminense in January"]. ''BBC Sport''. 4 December 2012.</ref> On 5 December, it was announced that Mikel John Obi had agreed to extended his Chelsea contract until summer 2017.<ref>[http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3001387/title/five-more-years-for-mikel "Five more years for Mikel"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121207224250/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3001387/title/five-more-years-for-mikel |date=7 December 2012 }}. Chelsea F.C. 5 December 2012.</ref>

On 5 December, Chelsea beat Nordsjælland 6–1 to [[List of Chelsea F.C. records and statistics#Wins|record their biggest-ever Champions League win]] and Rafael Benítez's first win as manager, but due to other results, they were eliminated after finishing in third place, becoming the first reigning champions to exit the tournament at the group stage.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20522151 "Chelsea 6–1 Nordsjaelland"]. ''BBC Sport''. 5 December 2012.</ref> On 8 December, Chelsea beat [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] 1–3 away with Fernando Torres scoring a [[2 (number)#In sports|brace]]. The victory was Chelsea's first league win in eight matches.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20564679 "Sunderland 1–3 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 8 December 2012.</ref>

Chelsea entered the [[2012 FIFA Club World Cup]] at the semi-final stage, where they beat [[CONCACAF]] champions [[C.F. Monterrey|Monterrey]] of Mexico 3–1 on 13 December,<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20658956 "Chelsea 3–1 Monterrey"]. ''BBC Sport''. 13 December 2012.</ref> before losing 1–0 in the final to [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] of Brazil in the [[International Stadium Yokohama|Yokohama Stadium]] three days later. [[Gary Cahill]] was sent off in injury time for violent conduct towards Corinthians' [[Emerson Sheik|Emerson]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20746503 "Chelsea 0–1 Corinthians"]. ''BBC Sport''. 16 December 2012.</ref>

The club returned to England with a 5–1 home victory in the League Cup against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] on 19 December, coming from a goal down at half-time to reach the semi-finals of the tournament.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20690782 "Leeds United 1–5 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 19 December 2012.</ref> The club's first Premier League match since the Club World Cup was an 8–0 victory over [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on 23 December,<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20745787 "Chelsea 8–0 Aston Villa"]. ''BBC Sport''. 23 December 2012.</ref> followed by a 0–1 win at Norwich City's [[Carrow Road]] three days later.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20779143 "Norwich 0–1 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 26 December 2012.</ref> A third consecutive Premier League victory was confirmed in the last match of 2012, which saw Frank Lampard score twice as Chelsea came from behind to win 1–2 away to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on 30 December, ending the Liverpool-based club's unbeaten home season.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20830257 "Everton 1–2 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 30 December 2012.</ref>

===January===
[[File:Demba Ba Sinsheim.jpg|thumb|right|200px|{{center|Senegalese forward [[Demba Ba]] was signed by Chelsea for £7 million from [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] on 2 January.}}]]
Chelsea made their first purchase of the January transfer window on 2 January by triggering the release clause in the contract of [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]'s Senegalese forward [[Demba Ba]]. Ba, who had scored 13 times in the season for his former club, was signed for £7 million.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130419192855/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/20890803|title="Demba Ba: Chelsea trigger Newcastle striker's release clause"}}. ''BBC Sport''. 2 January 2013.</ref> On the same day, Chelsea sold striker [[Daniel Sturridge]] to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] for an undisclosed fee reported to be £12 million. Sturridge played 96 games for Chelsea in three-and-a-half seasons, scoring 24 goals.<ref name="Sturridge Liverpool">{{cite web | url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3025002/title/sturridge-departs-for-liverpool | title=Sturridge departs for Liverpool | publisher=Chelsea F.C | date=2 January 2013 | access-date=6 January 2013 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130106031928/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3025002/title/sturridge-departs-for-liverpool | archive-date=6 January 2013}}</ref>

The year opened with a 0–1 home defeat to bottom-of-the-table West London rivals QPR, with the goal coming from former Chelsea winger [[Shaun Wright-Phillips]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20843072 "Chelsea 0–1 QPR"]. ''BBC Sport''. 2 January 2013.</ref> However, Chelsea made progress in the third round of the [[2012–13 FA Cup|FA Cup]], where they beat [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] 1–5 away at [[St Mary's Stadium|St Mary's]] on 5 January. Ba scored twice on his debut, while [[Frank Lampard]] scored his 193rd goal, moving him equal to [[Kerry Dixon]] as Chelsea's second-highest goalscorer of all time.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20863303 "Southampton 1–5 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 5 January 2013.</ref>

On 9 January, two defensive mistakes from defender [[Branislav Ivanović]] caused a 0–2 home loss in the League Cup first semi-final leg tie against Swansea City.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20886408 "Chelsea 0–2 Swansea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 9 January 2013.</ref> In their next Premier League match, on 12 January, Chelsea ended Stoke City's 17-game unbeaten home run by winning 0–4 away. Lampard's converted penalty, his 194th goal, moved him above Dixon's total.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20919045 "Stoke 0–4 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 12 January 2013.</ref> However, the following home match against Southampton on 16 January saw Chelsea give away a 2–0 half-time lead, opened by Ba's first Premier League goal, to draw 2–2.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20955084 "Chelsea 2–2 Southampton"]. ''BBC Sport''. 16 January 2013.</ref> The Blues then defeated [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|London rivals]] [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] 2–1 on 20 January, with early goals from [[Juan Mata]] and Frank Lampard cutting Chelsea's deficit behind second-place Manchester City to six points.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21002559 "Chelsea 2–1 Arsenal"]. ''BBC Sport''. 20 January 2013.</ref>

On 23 January, Chelsea drew the second leg of their League Cup semi-final against Swansea City, which sent Swansea through to the final. Chelsea's [[Eden Hazard]] was given a straight red card for an alleged violent attack on a Swansea ballboy.<ref>{{cite news|last=Doyle|first=Paul|title=Swansea City v Chelsea – as it happened|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jan/23/swansea-city-chelsea-live-mbm|access-date=24 January 2013|newspaper=The Guardian|date=24 January 2013}}</ref>

In the Fourth Round of the FA Cup, on 27 January, Chelsea went behind twice before a late [[Fernando Torres]] equaliser forced a replay against fellow West London club [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] of [[Npower League One|League One]].<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jan/27/brentford-chelsea-fa-cup-report "Brentford 2–2 Chelsea"]. ''The Guardian''. 27 January 2013.</ref> Chelsea's final Premier League game of the month, played on 30 January, saw them draw 2–2 for a second time in a week, conceding a 0–2 lead in the final three minutes away to Reading. Despite drawing, Frank Lampard's goal in the game made him the first midfielder in Premier League history to score ten or more goals in ten consecutive seasons.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21156120 "Reading 2–2 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 30 January 2013.</ref>

===February===
On 2 February, Chelsea lost their first away game since 1 December, losing 3–2 to Newcastle United, for whom [[Moussa Sissoko]] scored a late winner.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21209228 "Newcastle 3–2 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 2 February 2013.</ref> On 6 February, [[Ashley Cole]] became the first Chelsea player to earn 100 England caps when he played in a friendly against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]].<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/feb/06/england-brazil-international-friendly "England 2–1 Brazil"]. ''The Guardian''. 6 February 2013.</ref> On 9 February, Chelsea defeated Wigan Athletic 4–1 to go within four points of second-placed Manchester City, with [[Marko Marin]] scoring for the first time. His goal was the club's 100th of the season in all competitions<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130210052906/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/21311509 "Chelsea 4–1 Wigan"]. ''BBC Sport''. 9 February 2013.</ref>

Chelsea won their first [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] match since the 2002–03 season on 14 February, beating [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]] 0–1 at the [[Generali Arena]] through a late Oscar goal.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21448051 "Sparta Prague 0–1 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 14 February 2013.</ref> Three days later, Chelsea triumphed in their FA Cup replay match against Brentford, reaching the fifth round of the FA Cup.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21448628 "Chelsea 4–0 Brentford"]. ''BBC Sport''. 17 February 2013.</ref> In the second leg against Sparta Prague on 21 February, an injury time equaliser from Eden Hazard prevented the game from going to extra time by putting the club through 2–1 on aggregate.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21455163 "Chelsea 1–1 Sparta Prague (agg 2–1)"]. ''BBC Sport''. 21 February 2013.</ref>

On 24 February, Chelsea lost away to Manchester City, with Frank Lampard missing a second half penalty as the club lost 2–0.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21489693 "Manchester City 2–0 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 24 February 2013.</ref> In their last game of the month, on 27 February, Chelsea won away in their FA Cup 5th round tie against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] with second-half goals from [[Ramires]] and [[Victor Moses]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21515665 "Middlesbrough 0–2 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 27 February 2013.</ref>

===March===
Chelsea began the month with a 1–0 home win over West Bromwich Albion on 2 March, with Demba Ba scoring the only goal of the match.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21556758 "Chelsea 1–0 West Brom"]. ''BBC Sport''. 2 March 2013.</ref> On 7 March 2013, Chelsea lost the first leg of their [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League knockout phase|last 16 Europa League]] tie away against [[FC Steaua București|Steaua București]], with [[Ryan Bertrand]] conceding a penalty which was converted as the only goal of the match.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21611969 "Steaua Buch't 1–0 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 7 March 2013.</ref> In the 6th round of the FA Cup against Manchester United at [[Old Trafford]], Chelsea conceded two early goals before a second half comeback with goals by Ramires and Eden Hazard earned a home replay.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21646425 "Man Utd 2–2 Chelsea"]. ''BBC Sport''. 10 March 2013.</ref> Chelsea managed to overturn their Europa League deficit with a 3–1 victory to advance 3–2 on aggregate, in a match in which Fernando Torres scored the winning goal.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21696158 "Chelsea 3–1 Steaua Buch't (agg 3–2)"]. ''BBC Sport''. 14 March 2013.</ref>

===April===
April began with the FA Cup replay to Manchester United, winning it 1–0 thanks to a spectacular second half Demba Ba goal.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21921311 "Chelsea 1–0 Man Utd"]. ''BBC Sport''. 1 April 2013.</ref> Three days later, the club won their first leg Europa League tie against Russian side [[FC Rubin Kazan|Rubin Kazan]] 3–1 with two goals from [[Fernando Torres]] and one from Victor Moses.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21963641 "Chelsea 3–1 Rubin Kazan"]. ''BBC Sport''. 4 April 2013.</ref> With their third game in only seven days, Chelsea played [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] in the Premier League and came back down from 0–1 to win 2–1, the winner scored by [[Branislav Ivanović]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21986337 "Chelsea 2–1 Sunderland"]. ''BBC Sport''. 7 April 2013.</ref> Chelsea then played the second leg against Rubin Kazan on 11 April, losing 3–2 on the night but winning 5–4 on aggregate, sending them into the semi-finals of the competition.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22023533 "Rubin Kazan 3–2 Chelsea (agg 4–5)"]. ''BBC Sport''. 11 April 2013.</ref> On 14 April, Chelsea met Manchester City in the FA cup semi-finals, where they lost 1–2 and were thus eliminated.<ref>[http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3144013/title/match-report-chelsea-1-manchester-city-2 "Match report: Chelsea 1 Manchester City 2"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130416031802/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3144013/title/match-report-chelsea-1-manchester-city-2 |date=16 April 2013 }}. Chelsea F.C. 14 April 2013.</ref>

===May===
On 11 May, [[Frank Lampard]] broke Chelsea's all-time goal-scoring record by scoring two against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], earning him his 203rd goal for Chelsea. On 15 May, Chelsea won the [[2013 UEFA Europa League Final|Europa League final]] 1–2 against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Phil|last=McNulty|work=BBC Sport|title=Benfica 1–2 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22445388|date=15 May 2013|access-date=17 May 2013}}</ref> The day after Chelsea won the Europa League, Lampard signed a one-year contract extension with Chelsea.<ref>{{cite news|work=BBC Sport|title=Chelsea's Frank Lampard signs one-year contract|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22548313|date=16 May 2013|access-date=9 June 2013}}</ref> On 19 May, Chelsea ended the season with a 2–1 home-win against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]],<ref>{{cite news|work=BBC Sport|title=Chelsea 2–1 Everton|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22499152|date=19 May 2013|access-date=9 June 2013}}</ref> finishing in third place and qualifying for the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League group stage|2013–14 Champions League]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2021}}

Chelsea then went to an post-season trip to the United States, where they would meet Manchester City in two friendly matches. Chelsea's first match ended in disappointment as they let slip a three-goal lead at [[Busch Stadium]] in [[St. Louis]], [[Missouri]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130629133824/http://www.itv.com/sport/football/article/2013-05-24/match-report-chelsea-3-4-man-city-city-comeback-thrills-crowd-on-us-post-season-tour/|title="Match report: Chelsea 3–4 Man City"}}. [[ITV (TV network)|ITV]]. 24 May 2013.</ref> [[Rafael Benítez]]'s last game in charge for the Blues ended in a 3–5 defeat to Manchester City at [[Yankee Stadium]] in New York City on 25 May. It was also the last game for [[Paulo Ferreira]], who retired after the match, as well as [[Yossi Benayoun]]'s final match in a Chelsea shirt.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3191236/match-report-chelsea-3-manchester-city-5 |title=Match report: Chelsea 3 Manchester City 5 |publisher=Chelsea F.C |date=26 May 2013|access-date=7 June 2013}}</ref>

On 26 May, Chelsea announced that they had agreed to play in the inaugural Guinness [[International Champions Cup]] in the U.S. – Chelsea will join [[A.C. Milan|Milan]], [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]], [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], Everton and the [[LA Galaxy]] in the competition.<ref>[http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3191221/title/chelsea-to-play-in-stateside-tournament "Chelsea to play in Stateside tournament"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607071633/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3191221/title/chelsea-to-play-in-stateside-tournament |date=7 June 2013 }}. Chelsea F.C. 26 May 2013.</ref> On 28 May, Rafael Benítez was released from his contract with Chelsea to become the new manager of Italian side [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3193668/title/rafael-benitez |title=Rafael Benítez |publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=28 May 2013|access-date=7 June 2013}}</ref>
